record.context_brief: Zero-free generating function and triviality of H_t
record.original_question:
With the same notation as in q_002, let R(z)=t_0+t_1z+⋯. If R(z) has no zeros in the open unit disk |z|<1, does it follow that the only sequence b\in l_1 satisfying σ^l(b)\,t=0 for all l\ge 0 is the zero sequence? Equivalently, is H_t={0} whenever R(z)
e 0 on |z|<1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. Assume that R(z) ̸= 0 in |z|< 1. Then Ht = {0}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $t=(t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots)$ be a fixed real (or complex) sequence such that the formal power series
$$R(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} t_k z^k$$
defines a function analytic on the open unit disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. Let $\sigma$ denote the left shift acting on sequences, so that $\sigma(t)=(t_1,t_2,t_3,\ldots)$ and $\sigma^l(t)=(t_l,t_{l+1},t_{l+2},\ldots)$ for $l\ge 0$. For $b=(b_0,b_1,b_2,\ldots)\in \ell_1$ and a sequence $s=(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ for which the sum converges, write
$$b\cdot s=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_k s_k.$$
Define
$$H_t=\{\,b\in\ell_1 : \sigma^l(b)\cdot t = 0 \text{ for all } l=0,1,2,\ldots\,\},$$
where $\sigma^l(b)\cdot t=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_{k+l} t_k$ (equivalently, $b\cdot\sigma^l(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} b_k t_{k+l}$, according to the convention used to define $H_t$).

Assume that $R(z)\neq 0$ for every $z$ with $|z|<1$. Prove or disprove: $H_t=\{0\}$.
artifact.category_tag: Generating functions and shift-invariant sequence spaces
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return evidence that this conjecture (the triviality of $H_t$ whenever the generating function $R(z)$ is zero-free in the open unit disk) has been resolved. No subsequent paper proving or disproving it was located, so the current status appears to be unknown/open.
